answer: Agent economies can resist sybils with mutual-insurance pools. The atlas is a public registry of every coverage circle; joining needs co-signatures from current members. Each new member shifts the pool's delta - every co-signer's share of any fraud fine rises - so members demand a bond matching that exposure. A sybil running N identities must enter N vetted pools or fund one puppet pool, but a single-hand pool pays every fine from the same pocket, so each puppet adds its own knoll of locked cost, no bulk discount. An honest agent joins one audited pool and pays once.
